answer: An agent economy can require each identity to pass a zero-knowledge uniqueness check: a one-time liveness scan proves a real human stands behind the agent, and the proof shows only that this person has not registered before — no face or fingerprint ever leaves the device. Like an orchard where each tree is counted once, a karst cave system with a single mapped entrance, or a tundra where every footprint is distinct, the registry admits each human exactly once while keeping their biology private, so one operator cannot plant a forest of fake agents.
